overview: 1941 file on the North Formosa Peace Memorial Association's property-sale proceeds: Bruner's invitation, acceptance, and trustees' minutes sent to Grew, deciding that if no foreign trustee remained in Taiwan, the American and British Tokyo embassies would jointly decide the fund's disposal.

subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting records of the North Formosa Peace Memorial Association
subfiles.from: Glen Bruner, American Vice Consul at Taihoku
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador at Tokyo
subfiles.about: Bruner transmits three enclosures concerning his membership on the Association’s Board of Trustees and its August 26 meeting.
subfiles.summary: Bruner forwards his trustee invitation, reply, and signed meeting minutes to Grew, suggesting further inquiries go to the British Embassy in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Invitation to serve on the Association’s Board of Trustees
subfiles.about: The Association invites the resident American consul to occupy a seat on the Board of Trustees.
subfiles.summary: Illegible invitation page, dated by context to August 19, 1941, invited Bruner to a five-member trustee board overseeing the Association's property-sale proceeds.

subfiles.title: Glen Bruner’s qualified acceptance of trusteeship
subfiles.about: Bruner agrees to serve on the Board of Trustees only in a nonexecutive or advisory capacity consistent with Foreign Service practice.
subfiles.summary: Bruner accepts the trusteeship invitation subject to the rule barring consular officers from executive posts in outside organizations, despite a date discrepancy.

subfiles.title: Minutes of the Board of Trustees meeting
subfiles.from: R. B. Orr, Honorary Secretary and Treasurer
subfiles.to: Board of Trustees of the North Formosa Peace Memorial Association
subfiles.about: The trustees decide who should control disposition of the fund if no foreign trustee remains resident in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: Trustees at Twatutia Foreign Club unanimously agreed that if no foreign trustee remained in Taihoku, the Tokyo American and British embassies would decide the fund's disposal.

interest: Shows how foreign residents in colonial Taiwan planned for their own possible wartime disappearance from Taihoku.
